# Texas Solutions Truck Dispatch

> Texas Solutions is a US truck dispatch service for owner-operators and small fleets, based in Midland, Texas. Dispatch fee: 5% of weekly gross for OTR semi trucks, 8% for hotshots, 10% for box trucks and straight trucks. No flat rate, no setup fee, no monthly subscription, no forced loads. Also free trucking calculators (fuel cost, cost per mile, IFTA, HOS, load profitability and more), daily diesel prices by state, and a trucking blog. Texas Solutions is not a motor carrier or freight broker and does not guarantee loads, rates or earnings.

## Key facts
- Service: truck dispatch (load search, rate negotiation, broker setup packets, rate confirmations, lane planning)
- Semi truck dispatch fee (dry van, reefer, flatbed, step deck, power only): 5% of weekly gross, OTR - about $400-$500 per week on typical gross of $8,000-$10,000
- Hotshot dispatch fee: 8% of weekly gross, OTR - for example $560-$720 on a hypothetical $7,000-$9,000 week
- Box truck and straight truck dispatch fee: 10% of weekly gross, OTR - for example $700-$900 on a hypothetical $7,000-$9,000 week
- The fee is a percentage of weekly gross (what the truck earns hauling loads that week). No flat rate, no setup fee, no monthly subscription, no long-term contract, no forced loads
- Condition: Rates apply to OTR (over-the-road) operations. Local and regional work is quoted separately.
- Free trial: the first load is dispatched free
- Dispatchers available 24/7 (remote team across US time zones); works with brand-new MC authority from day one
- Back-office services: broker carrier packets, rate confirmations, invoicing and billing, detention and lumper collection, factoring setup, IFTA filing, DOT compliance help, MC authority setup
- Equipment dispatched: dry van, reefer, flatbed, step deck, power only, hotshot, box truck, straight truck
- Rough freight rates per mile (not guaranteed): flatbed $5-7, step deck $5-7, reefer $4-6, hotshot $4-5, dry van $3-5 (local or OTR), power only $3-5, box truck $1.80-3.20
- Area served: the contiguous 48 states (remote dispatchers across US time zones); office in Midland, Texas. Alaska and Hawaii-based carriers can ask about mainland operations
- Texas Solutions is a dispatch service. It is not a motor carrier or freight broker and does not guarantee loads, rates or earnings
- Phone: (838) 910-3147 | WhatsApp: +1 838 910 3147 (https://wa.me/18389103147) | Email: dispatch@texassolutions.co
- Address: 401 W Kentucky Ave, Midland, TX 79701
- Owner and CEO: Shehryar Joyia

## Free trucking calculators
- [Tools hub](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/tools.html): all calculators in one place
- [Dispatch fee calculator and free quote](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/estimate.html): dispatch fee by truck type, plus a quote request via WhatsApp
- [Truck fuel cost calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/truck-fuel-cost-calculator.html): MPG by truck type and load weight, trip fuel cost, cost per mile, daily diesel price by state
- [Cost Per Mile (CPM) Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/cost-per-mile-calculator.html): Free trucking cost per mile calculator for owner-operators: fixed and variable costs, your own driver pay shown separately, and cost per total mile and per loaded mile.
- [Load Profitability Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/load-profitability-calculator.html): Free load profitability calculator: revenue, dispatch and factoring fees, deadhead and return miles, your cost per mile and trip expenses give estimated profit, effective rate per mile and the rate you need.
- [Break-Even Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/break-even-calculator.html): Free break-even calculator for owner-operators: enter fixed costs, variable cost per mile and your freight rate to see the miles per month you need to break even, and your profit at your planned miles.
- [Deadhead Miles Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/deadhead-miles-calculator.html): Free deadhead miles calculator: see your deadhead percentage and effective rate per mile once empty miles are counted against a load's revenue.
- [Driver Pay Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/driver-pay-calculator.html): Free truck driver pay calculator: work out weekly, monthly and annual pay for per-mile, per-load, percentage of gross, or hourly pay models.
- [IFTA Mileage Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/ifta-mileage-calculator.html): Free IFTA mileage calculator: log miles driven and fuel purchased by state, see gallons consumed per jurisdiction, and estimate net taxable gallons for your own IFTA records.
- [Per Diem Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/per-diem-calculator.html): Free per diem calculator for truck drivers: estimate your annual per diem deduction and potential tax savings based on days on the road. Not tax advice.
- [Truck Loan Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/truck-loan-calculator.html): Free truck loan calculator: enter the truck price, down payment, interest rate and term to see your monthly payment, total interest and total cost.
- [Maintenance Budget Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/maintenance-budget-calculator.html): Free truck maintenance budget calculator: estimate a yearly and monthly repair reserve based on your truck's age and annual mileage.
- [Hours of Service (HOS) Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/hours-of-service-calculator.html): Free HOS calculator: estimate remaining drive time under the FMCSA 11-hour driving limit, 14-hour on-duty window and 60/7 or 70/8-day cycle limits. Planning tool only, not a legal record.
- [Freight Class Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/freight-class-calculator.html): Free freight class calculator: estimate NMFC freight class from length, width, height and weight using the standard density table. Estimate only, confirm with your carrier.
- [Fuel Surcharge Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/fuel-surcharge-calculator.html): Free trucking fuel surcharge calculator: base and current fuel price, agreed MPG and miles give surcharge per mile and total, using the per-mile, step-table or percentage method in your contract.
- [Detention Pay Calculator](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/detention-pay-calculator.html): Free truck detention pay calculator: enter arrival, appointment and release times, free time, hourly rate and billing increment to see eligible detention hours and estimated detention pay.

## Guides (blog)
- [Truck Loads and Load Boards: How They Work for Carriers](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/truck-loads-and-load-boards-guide.html): A load board is an online marketplace where brokers and shippers post truck loads and carriers search for freight that fits their equipment and lanes. Carriers filter by origin, destination, equipment and date, check the broker's credit and payment history, then call or message to negotiate and book. Paid boards like DAT and Truckstop add more loads and tools, while free boards have fewer features.
- [Non-CDL Box Truck and Hotshot Loads: Weight Rules and How to Find Freight](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/non-cdl-box-truck-and-hotshot-loads.html): Often yes, if you stay under the federal CDL thresholds. A single truck generally needs a CDL at a GVWR or actual weight of 26,001 lbs or more, and a combination generally needs a Class A CDL at 26,001 lbs or more combined when the trailer is rated or weighs over 10,000 lbs. Placarded hazmat requires a CDL at any size. Confirm with FMCSA and your state before you buy or load.
- [How to Start a Hotshot Business: Truck, Trailer, Authority and Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-start-a-hotshot-business.html): Pick a heavy-duty pickup and flatbed or gooseneck trailer that match the freight you plan to haul, check whether the combination's weight ratings require a CDL, then get a USDOT number, MC operating authority, a BOC-3 and commercial insurance. Once your authority is active, book loads through load boards, brokers or a hotshot dispatch company.
- [How to Start a Box Truck Business: Authority, Equipment and First Loads](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-start-a-box-truck-business.html): Choose a box truck that fits the freight you want (most owner-operators pick a 26 ft truck with a liftgate), form your business, get a USDOT number and MC operating authority, file a BOC-3, and buy the insurance brokers require. Then set up invoicing and start booking loads through load boards, brokers or a dispatcher who works with new authority.
- [How to Get Loads Without a Broker: Direct Freight Explained](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-get-loads-without-a-broker.html): Owner-operators get loads without a broker by working directly with shippers, winning dedicated lanes or contracts, and using carrier platforms such as Amazon Relay. Direct freight can pay more and be steadier, but it takes time to win, often pays on longer terms, and usually requires a clean safety record and proven on-time service.
- [How to Choose a Fuel Card for Truckers: What to Compare](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-choose-a-fuel-card-for-truckers.html): Start with where you actually fuel, then compare how the discount is calculated (retail-minus or cost-plus), which truck stops accept the card, every fee, whether it is credit or prepaid, and how well it reports gallons by state for IFTA. The best fuel card for truckers is the one that fits your lanes and paperwork, not the one with the biggest advertised number.
- [How to Become an Owner-Operator: Lease-On or Your Own MC](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-become-an-owner-operator.html): To become an owner-operator you need the right license and experience for your truck, a truck you own or lease, and a way to haul freight: either leasing on to an existing carrier or getting your own USDOT number and MC authority. Running your own MC also means insurance, broker setup, compliance and a plan for finding loads, which is where a dispatch service can help.
- [How Much Do Hotshot Drivers Make? A Realistic Look at Gross and Net](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-much-do-hotshot-drivers-make.html): Hotshot owner-operator income depends on miles, rates and costs. As a hypothetical example, hotshots might gross about $7,000 to $9,000 a week, which is not guaranteed. After fuel, insurance, equipment payments, maintenance and fees, our worked examples keep about 50 to 58 percent of gross before taxes, and real results can be lower.
- [How Much Do Box Truck Owner-Operators Make? Gross, Costs and Net](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-much-do-box-truck-owner-operators-make.html): It varies widely with miles, rates and costs. As a hypothetical example, box trucks might gross about $7,000 to $9,000 a week, though that is not guaranteed. After fuel, insurance, truck payments, maintenance and fees, our worked examples keep about 42 to 49 percent of gross before taxes, and real results can be lower.
- [How Does Truck Dispatching Work? A Carrier's Step-by-Step Guide](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-does-truck-dispatching-work.html): A truck dispatcher works for the carrier, not the shipper. After onboarding your authority, insurance and preferences, the dispatcher searches for loads that fit your truck and lanes, negotiates the rate with the broker, and books the load only after you approve it. The dispatcher then handles paperwork, check calls and invoicing support, and charges a fee, usually a percentage of the truck's weekly gross.
- [Freight Dispatcher vs Truck Dispatcher: Same Job, Different Name](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/freight-dispatcher-vs-truck-dispatcher.html): For a US carrier, yes. Freight dispatcher, truck dispatcher, trucking dispatcher and cargo dispatcher are different labels for the same carrier-side role: someone who finds loads for your truck, negotiates the rate, and books freight under your authority after you approve it. The real differences to watch are who the person works for and what services the fee includes, not the job title.
- [Dry Van, Reefer, Flatbed and Power Only Loads: Finding and Pricing Them](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/dry-van-reefer-flatbed-power-only-loads.html): Rate per mile depends on the lane, season, distance, how much equipment is available in the pickup market, and the extra work or cost the load involves. Flatbed and step deck usually pay more for securement and tarping, reefer pays more for temperature control, and dry van and power only face the most competition. All rates vary and are not guaranteed.
- [Dispatch Service Percentage vs Flat Fee: Which Is Better?](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/dispatch-percentage-vs-flat-fee.html): A percentage fee rises and falls with what your truck earns, so you pay less in slow weeks and the dispatcher is motivated to book better-paying freight. A flat fee is predictable but costs the same in a bad week. The right choice depends on your weekly gross, how steady your freight is, and whether the offer hides extra charges or contracts.
- [Box Truck Contracts: How to Get Them and Where Amazon Relay Fits](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/box-truck-contracts-how-to-get-them.html): Most box truck contracts grow out of a track record: on-time spot loads that turn into repeat lanes with brokers, then dedicated or contract work with brokers, shippers and local businesses. Have your authority, insurance and paperwork ready, approach shippers whose freight fits a box truck, and protect your service record. Amazon Relay is another option for carriers with their own authority who meet its current requirements.
- [Best Load Boards for Hotshot and How to Find Hotshot Loads](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/best-load-boards-for-hotshot.html): No single load board is best for every hotshot. Large boards such as DAT, Truckstop and 123Loadboard all carry hotshot and partial flatbed freight, and the right one depends on your lanes, deck length and weight limits. Test a board, track the loads you actually book and what they pay, and keep the one that earns its cost.
- [Best Load Boards for Box Trucks and How to Find Box Truck Loads](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/best-load-boards-for-box-trucks.html): There is no single best load board for every box truck. Large general boards such as DAT, Truckstop and 123Loadboard all let you filter for straight or box truck freight, and the right choice depends on the lanes you run and how much box truck freight shows up there. Many owner-operators test a board for a month, track the loads they actually book, and keep the one that pays.
- [Is a Truck Dispatcher Worth It? Self-Dispatch vs Dispatch Service](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/is-a-truck-dispatcher-worth-it.html): A truck dispatcher is worth it when the fee costs less than the value you get back in better rates, fewer empty miles, less paperwork and more time to drive or rest. If you already have strong broker relationships and enjoy booking freight, self-dispatch can work well. Compare the fee with your own time and results before you decide.
- [How to Start a Trucking Company and Get Loads With New Authority](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-start-a-trucking-company.html): Register with FMCSA for a USDOT number and MC operating authority, file a BOC-3, register for UCR, get the required insurance, and set up IRP plates, IFTA, an ELD and a drug and alcohol program where they apply. Then set up factoring and broker accounts. With new authority, expect some brokers to say no at first, and focus on those that accept new carriers.
- [How to Negotiate Freight Rates and Increase Your Rate Per Mile](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-negotiate-freight-rates.html): Know your cost per mile and your minimum rate before you call. Ask about the load details, counter above your target with a clear reason, and be ready to walk away. Include deadhead miles in your math so the rate covers every mile you drive.
- [How to Find Loads for Your Truck: A Practical Guide for Owner-Operators](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-find-loads-for-your-truck.html): Most owner-operators find loads through a mix of load boards, direct broker relationships, direct shippers and dispatch services. The highest paying loads are usually the ones that pay well per total mile, including deadhead, and leave you in a market with good outbound freight. A dispatcher can search, negotiate and book loads for you under your own authority.
- [How to Choose a Truck Dispatcher and Avoid Dispatch Scams](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-choose-a-truck-dispatcher-avoid-scams.html): Check that the dispatcher has a real business presence, a written agreement, clear fees and no upfront payment demands. Ask for references from current carriers and look at independent reviews. Walk away from anyone who guarantees income, asks you to haul under their authority or pressures you to accept loads.
- [How Much Do Owner-Operators Make? Gross vs Net Explained](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-much-do-owner-operators-make.html): It varies widely. What an owner-operator makes is weekly gross minus fuel, truck costs, insurance, maintenance, fees and taxes. In our example, a semi grossing $7,200 in a week keeps about $3,000 before taxes. Your own result depends on your rate per mile, miles, costs and home time.
- [Broker Setup, Rate Confirmations and Spot vs Contract Rates](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/broker-setup-rate-confirmation-spot-vs-contract.html): To get set up with a broker, a carrier completes the broker's carrier packet, usually online. It typically includes your MC authority, certificate of insurance, W-9, a signed broker-carrier agreement and payment details. Once approved, the broker can send you a rate confirmation for a load.
- [What Is Deadhead in Trucking and How to Reduce It](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/what-is-deadhead-in-trucking-how-to-reduce-it.html): Deadhead is driving a truck empty, without paid freight, usually to reach a pickup or return from a delivery. Deadhead miles burn fuel and use up legal driving hours while earning nothing, so they lower your effective rate per mile. You can cut them by planning the next load before you deliver, and by choosing lanes with strong return freight.
- [What Is a Good Rate Per Mile in Trucking in 2026?](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/what-is-a-good-rate-per-mile-trucking-2026.html): A good rate per mile is one that covers your total cost per mile, including deadhead, and leaves profit. As a rough guide in 2026, flatbed and step deck often pay about $5-7 a mile, reefer $4-6, hotshot $4-5, dry van and power only $3-5, and box trucks $1.80-3.20, depending on lane, season and market.
- [Truck Dispatcher vs Freight Broker: The Real Difference](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/truck-dispatcher-vs-freight-broker.html): A truck dispatcher works for the carrier: they find and negotiate loads for the carrier's trucks and are paid by the carrier, usually a percentage of gross. A freight broker works between shippers and carriers: they need their own FMCSA broker authority and a surety bond, and earn the margin between what the shipper pays and what the carrier is paid.
- [IFTA for Owner-Operators: How to File Quarterly Returns](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/ifta-for-owner-operators-how-to-file.html): The International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) lets carriers running across US states and Canadian provinces file one quarterly fuel tax return with their base jurisdiction. Returns are due the last day of the month after each quarter ends: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31.
- [How to Get Your MC Number and Trucking Authority](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-to-get-mc-number-authority-owner-operator.html): To get an MC number you register with FMCSA for a USDOT number, apply for for-hire operating authority (the MC number), file a BOC-3 process agent, and have your insurer file proof of at least $750,000 liability coverage for general freight. Authority typically goes active a few weeks after everything is on file.
- [Hours of Service Rules Explained: 11, 14 and 70-Hour](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/hours-of-service-rules-explained-11-14-70-hour.html): Property-carrying drivers may drive up to 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty, may not drive beyond the 14th hour after coming on duty, must take a 30-minute break after 8 cumulative hours of driving, and cannot drive after 60 hours in 7 days or 70 hours in 8 days. A 34-hour off-duty restart resets the weekly cycle.
- [Freight Factoring for Owner-Operators: How It Works](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/freight-factoring-for-owner-operators-explained.html): In freight factoring, you sell your unpaid invoices to a factoring company, which advances you most of the invoice value right away, often 80-95%, and pays the rest, minus its fee, when the broker pays. Fees commonly run from about 1% to 5% of the invoice, depending on volume, terms and whether the deal is recourse or non-recourse.
- [Dry Van vs Reefer vs Flatbed: Which Trailer Pays Best?](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/dry-van-vs-reefer-vs-flatbed-which-trailer.html): As a rough guide, flatbed and step deck loads often pay about $5-7 a mile, reefer about $4-6, and dry van about $3-5, depending on lane, season and whether the run is local or OTR. Higher rates come with more work: tarping and securement on flatbed, temperature and appointment rules on reefer. Dry van has the most freight and the most competition.
- [Cost of Running a Semi Truck Per Mile (2026 Breakdown)](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/cost-of-running-a-semi-truck-per-mile.html): The American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) found the industry-average cost to operate a truck in 2025 was $2.336 per mile, or $1.854 per mile excluding fuel. Your own cost depends on your truck payment, insurance, fuel, maintenance and how many miles you run, so calculate it yourself before accepting rates.
- [Best Load Boards for Owner-Operators and How to Use Them](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/best-load-boards-for-owner-operators.html): Popular load boards include DAT One, Truckstop and 123Loadboard, plus specialty boards for hotshot, flatbed and power only. The best one depends on your equipment and lanes: look for fresh postings, rate data, broker credit information, and easy filtering. Many carriers use two boards and vet every broker before booking.
- [How Much Does a Truck Dispatcher Cost in 2026?](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/how-much-does-a-truck-dispatcher-cost.html): Most independent truck dispatchers charge a percentage of the truck's weekly gross, usually somewhere between 3% and 10%. Texas Solutions charges 5% for OTR semi trucks, 8% for hotshots and 10% for box trucks and straight trucks, with no flat rate, no setup fee and no monthly subscription.
- [Hotshot Trucking Rates Per Mile, Fuel and Dispatch (2026)](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/hotshot-trucking-rates-per-mile-fuel-and-dispatch.html): Hotshot loads often pay roughly $4 to $5 a mile, depending on lane, urgency and season. A 1-ton diesel pulling a gooseneck typically gets about 13-14 mpg empty and 8-10 mpg loaded. Texas Solutions dispatches hotshots for 8% of weekly gross, OTR, with no flat rate.
- [Diesel Prices by State: How Truckers Cut Fuel Cost Per Mile](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/diesel-prices-by-state-cut-fuel-cost-per-mile.html): Fuel cost per mile equals the diesel price divided by your miles per gallon. A loaded semi averaging about 6.3 mpg with diesel at $6.00 a gallon spends about $0.95 per mile on fuel. Diesel can differ by more than $2 a gallon between the cheapest and most expensive states, so where you fuel up matters.
- [Box Truck Dispatch: How to Find Loads and What It Really Costs](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/blog/box-truck-dispatch-find-loads-and-costs.html): Box truck owner-operators find loads through load boards, direct broker relationships and dispatch services. A 26 ft diesel box truck typically gets about 8.5-11 mpg. Texas Solutions dispatches box trucks and straight trucks for 10% of weekly gross, OTR, with no flat rate.

## Dispatch services
- [Box Truck Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/box-truck-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides box truck dispatch for owner-operators and small fleets across the contiguous 48 states. Dispatchers search and negotiate loads, complete broker setups and keep paperwork organized. The fee is 10% of weekly gross for OTR box trucks and straight trucks, with no flat rate, no setup fee and your approval on every load.
- [Hotshot Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/hotshot-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions is a hotshot dispatch company for owner-operators across the contiguous 48 states. Dispatchers find expedited and partial loads, negotiate rates that often run $4-5 a mile, and handle broker paperwork. The dispatch fee is 8% of weekly gross for OTR hotshots, with no flat rate.
- [Flatbed & Step Deck Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/flatbed-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides flatbed and step deck dispatch for owner-operators and small fleets across the contiguous 48 states. Dispatchers find open-deck loads that often pay $5-7 a mile, confirm dimensions, weight and tarping, and handle broker paperwork. The fee is 5% of weekly gross for OTR semis, with no flat rate.
- [Dry Van Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/dry-van-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides dry van dispatch for owner-operators and small fleets across the contiguous 48 states. Dispatchers plan lanes to reduce deadhead, negotiate every load and handle broker paperwork. Dry van loads run roughly $3-5 a mile depending on local or OTR lanes, and the dispatch fee is 5% of weekly gross for OTR semis.
- [Reefer Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/reefer-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides reefer dispatch for owner-operators and small fleets across the contiguous 48 states. Dispatchers find temperature-controlled loads, confirm temperature and appointment requirements with brokers and handle paperwork. The fee is 5% of weekly gross for OTR reefer semis, with no flat rate.
- [Power Only Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/power-only-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides power only dispatch for owner-operators with a tractor and no trailer. Dispatchers find preloaded and drop-and-hook loads, negotiate the rate and handle broker paperwork. The fee is 5% of weekly gross for OTR operations.
- [Owner-Operator Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/owner-operator-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions is a dispatch service for owner-operators and small fleets. It handles load search, rate negotiation, broker communication and paperwork for 5% of weekly gross on OTR semis, 8% on hotshots and 10% on box trucks, with no flat rate, no upfront fee, no long-term contract and no forced loads.
- [New Authority Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/dispatch-for-new-authority.html): Texas Solutions dispatches carriers with brand-new MC authority from day one. Dispatchers send your carrier packets, find brokers that accept new MC numbers, negotiate every load and handle rate confirmations and invoicing, 24/7. Your first load is dispatched free; after that the fee is 5% of weekly gross for semis, 8% for hotshots and 10% for box trucks.
- [Back-Office Services](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/trucking-back-office-services.html): Texas Solutions handles trucking back-office work alongside dispatch: broker carrier packets and carrier setup with brokers, rate confirmations, invoicing and billing, detention and lumper fee collection, factoring setup, IFTA filing, DOT compliance help and MC authority setup. Dispatchers are available 24/7, and the first load is dispatched free.
- [Semi Truck Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/semi-truck-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions provides semi truck dispatch services across the contiguous 48 states for owner-operators and small fleets running dry van, reefer, flatbed, step deck and power only. Dispatchers search loads, negotiate every rate, handle broker setups and plan lanes around your home time, for 5% of weekly gross on OTR semis with no flat rate.
- [Small Fleet Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/small-fleet-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions dispatches small fleets and small trucking companies with roughly 2 to 10 trucks. Each truck is planned on its own equipment, lanes and driver home time, and the owner gets one point of contact and a weekly summary. The fee is per truck: 5% of weekly gross for semis, 8% for hotshots and 10% for box trucks, with no fleet setup fee.
- [MC Number & Authority Setup](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/trucking-authority-setup.html): An MC number is the motor carrier number FMCSA issues with for-hire operating authority, which lets you haul regulated freight for other companies across state lines. Texas Solutions helps new carriers through each step: USDOT and MC applications, the BOC-3 process agent filing, insurance filings, UCR and broker packets. Government and insurance costs are paid by the carrier, and we start dispatching as soon as your authority is active.
- [Texas Truck Dispatch](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/texas-truck-dispatch.html): Texas Solutions is a nationwide truck dispatch company with its head office at 401 W Kentucky Ave, Midland, Texas. For Texas carriers it dispatches lanes out of Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio, Laredo, El Paso and the Permian Basin, and anywhere those loads lead, for 5% of weekly gross on semis, 8% on hotshots and 10% on box trucks.
- [What a Truck Dispatcher Does](https://dispatch.texassolutions.co/what-does-a-truck-dispatcher-do.html): A truck dispatcher finds and books freight for a carrier's trucks: searching load boards and brokers, negotiating rates, confirming loads with the driver, completing broker setup paperwork and organizing rate confirmations. Independent dispatchers usually charge a percentage of weekly gross; Texas Solutions charges 5% for OTR semis, 8% for hotshots and 10% for box trucks.
